top_stories.title: Bitcoin Falls Below $82K-83K After Hot September Inflation Data
points: September consumer prices rose 3.7% year-over-year (above the 3.6% forecast and up from 3.4% in August), with a 9.1% gasoline surge accounting for over half the monthly gain.
Bitcoin fell below $82,000-$83,000 as the data reduced prospects for near-term Fed rate cuts.
Fed rate hike odds for the October 27-28 meeting surged to near 50% (doubling from 22%), while the 10-year Treasury yield climbed near 24-year highs at 5.3%.
Risk-free Treasury bonds now compete directly with Bitcoin's zero yield, and higher rates make borrowing expensive, draining speculative capital from crypto assets.
Producer Price Index due Thursday is the next key inflation test that could further move Fed expectations and crypto markets.

items.title: Ethereum Foundation Warns AI Could Break Crypto Signatures
points: An Ethereum Foundation researcher warns AI could break crypto's ECDSA signature scheme (the cryptographic math that secures private keys and proves wallet ownership) before quantum computers do, prompting industry action.

items.title: Ledger Hardware Wallet Supply Chain Breach
points: Ledger asked resellers across seven Asian markets to pull hardware wallets after a suspected $86 million drain linked to implanted malware in devices.
A German customer discovered a physical implant in a Ledger device, prompting European electronics chain MediaMarkt Saturn to halt all Ledger sales.
The attack bypasses cold storage security (keeping crypto offline for safety), representing a supply chain compromise rather than a software vulnerability.

items.title: Regulatory and Legal Pressures on Crypto Figures
points: BitMEX is being sued in a UK court for $27 million in Bitcoin over unlicensed derivatives trading, covering 1,053 loss-making perpetual swap trades (leveraged bets on price without owning the underlying asset) from 2018-2022.
Hex founder Richard Heart was detained in Istanbul on an Interpol Red Notice, with authorities seizing cash, phones, jewelry, and firearms from his Beşiktaş residence.
These enforcement actions signal a tightening regulatory environment against unregistered exchanges and high-profile crypto figures.

items.title: White House Exploring Adding More Bitcoin to Reserves
points: The White House is reportedly exploring adding to its existing Bitcoin holdings, suggesting potential institutional acceptance of crypto as a reserve asset.
If pursued, this would position Bitcoin alongside traditional reserve assets held by the U.S. government, a significant policy shift.

items.title: Standard Chartered Launches Bitcoin Trading in UAE
points: Standard Chartered bank launched Bitcoin trading services in the United Arab Emirates, providing institutional-grade access to cryptocurrency.
The move signals growing mainstream financial adoption in the Gulf region and marks a major bank's entry into regulated crypto markets.
